text:
maria_ops: Heads-up: I'm pausing the BIOS 1.4.2 rollout for eu-west GPU racks. Seeing serial console resets on a small percentage of nodes during the flash step — roughly 12/420 (≈2.9%). Hangs show ECC/errors and kernel oops after reboot. Holding the rest of the batch.

jason_infra: any commonalities? hw model / BMC rev / rack?

maria_ops: All affected are A100-8gpu nodes on rackpool-eu-west-3. BMC rev varies: v2.3 and v2.4. Flashing via kexec+fwupd. I pulled a raw BMC syslog from one node: 

maria_ops: ```
[2026-03-18T09:12:30Z] fw_flash: starting BIOS image write
[2026-03-18T09:12:38Z] bmc: serial-console: port drop detected, reinitializing
[2026-03-18T09:12:38Z] mca: [Hardware Error]: CPU cache ECC error, concluded recoverable
[2026-03-18T09:12:40Z] kernel: BUG: unable to handle kernel NULL pointer dereference at 00000000
[2026-03-18T09:12:42Z] kexec_core: trying to kexec_load: panic during image verify
```

liam_fw: Hmm. The timing suggests the BMC is toggling the console during the flash/UEFI variable write. We've seen vendor BMC fw that resets UART during NVRAM updates. Could be a race between BIOS commit and BMC watchdog.

eva_oncall: @maria_ops can you tag the affected hostnames? we'll drain and repro on a stuck node in the lab. Also we should pin capacity — move live jobs off those racks and failover to us-west-1 while we triage.

maria_ops: Tagged: eu3-gpu-104..eu3-gpu-115. Draining now. Will repro 1 node in lab (eu3-gpu-109).

jason_infra: Can you try flashing with --no-nvram-write or equivalent to see if it's the UEFI var write? Also test flashing with BMC in maintenance mode (disable watchdog) and run ipmitool remote serial redirection to watch.

maria_ops: Good call. Ran two quick experiments:
- Flash with nvram-skipped (vendor tool flag) -> node reboots cleanly, no serial drop.
- Flash with watchdog disabled via BMC -> still had a brief serial blip but no kernel oops.

liam_fw: That points at UEFI variable commit timing + BMC/WD interaction. Likely the BIOS update is issuing an SMM call that temporarily quiesces the UART and the BMC sees that as a failure and triggers reset. There's also an ECC burst logged — could be caused by the same transient or unrelated memory noise.

vendor-bmc-bot: Automated vendor note: Known issue in BMC v2.3/v2.4 where serial flush during SMR (SMM RAM) writes can trigger watchdog expiry. Patch available in v2.4.1 (pre-release). See https://vendor.example.com/alerts/SMR-UART-2026

jason_infra: If vendor has a pre-release, we should avoid mass upgrades. Action plan: 1) Rollback BIOS on the 12 affected nodes to 1.3.9; 2) Update runbook to include NV-RAM skip flag for eu-west batch until vendor patch is validated; 3) Open high-priority SR with vendor and request BMC patch; 4) Add a pre-upgrade step to set BMC watchdog threshold longer and block if BMC rev < 2.4.1.

maria_ops: I'll start rollback job for the 12 nodes and add a canary node in eu-west lab with v2.4.1 pre-release when vendor gives binary. I'll also create an infra ticket (#INC-2026-354) and attach logs.

eva_oncall: Moving live capacity off those racks + adjusting autoscaler to prefer us-west for new GPU allocations. Noting cost hit for cross-region traffic, but small short-term. :warning:

deploy-bot: CI:gpu-fleet-tests pipeline rerun queued due to drained hosts (build 4832).

jason_infra: Also update the scheduler tagging: add tag `bmc-potential-reset=eu-west-3-2026-03-18` so flows don't land there accidentally.

maria_ops: Done. Pushing runbook change to repo and adding blocked step in rollout automation to abort if BMC rev < 2.4.1. Will follow up with SR number once vendor responds.

liam_fw: If vendor patch is delayed, workaround options: 1) keep nvram-skip flag (but validate post-upgrade GUID entries); 2) sequence BIOS update to two-phase with a short delay after SMM commits; 3) schedule maintenance window with workload soak. Pros/cons documented in runbook.

maria_ops: Thanks all. I'll update the incident ticket and loop in support/ps. Closing the rollout for now. :white_check_mark:
